title: Associate Director, Operational Risk Management
descriptionHtml:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

About the team

The Global Risk team at Airwallex plays a critical role in enabling the company's growth by building a strong, scalable, and globally consistent approach to risk management.

The team works across the business to define risk appetite, develop frameworks and policies, support strategic decision-making, and provide oversight of key risks as Airwallex expands across products, markets, and regulatory environments.

You'll be part of a highly collaborative group that partners closely with Product, Engineering, Operations, Commercial, Financial Crime Compliance, Regulatory Compliance, and Legal teams to help Airwallex grow responsibly and with confidence.

This is a team where you'll tackle complex, high-impact challenges, shape how risk is managed at a global fintech, and help build the foundations for long-term scale.

How you'll make impact

You'll own the Group's Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) and Incident Management framework as part of the Second Line of Defence, and provide independent, consolidated oversight of how the First Line identifies, assesses, and manages risk across Group entities.

  • Own the Group RCSA and incident management frameworks: Maintain the methodologies, standards, policies, taxonomy, guidance, templates, and supporting procedures for the Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) and for identifying, recording, investigating, and reporting operational risk events, keeping them current and aligned with Group operating models, risk appetite, local entity requirements, and relevant regulatory expectations.

  • Drive consistency across the Group: Promote consistent risk assessment, incident classification, and ownership across business units and Group entities.

  • Provide independent review and challenge: Challenge First Line risk assessments, control ratings, incident classification, root-cause analysis, and remediation plans, ensuring they are timely, evidence-based, proportionate, and comparable across the business.

  • Govern the lifecycle and drive actions to closure: Support governance of RCSA frequency, approvals, and evidence standards, and track actions arising from RCSAs and incidents through to completion, escalating overdue items with clear accountability.

  • Turn data into insight and decision-ready MI: Analyse RCSA, incident, and loss data to identify trends, themes, and systemic control weaknesses, escalate repeat issues to the right owners and governance forums, and produce clear reporting and recommended actions for Operational Risk reporting, governance forums, and relevant risk management committees.

  • Support regulatory notification: Work with Regulatory Compliance, Regulatory Legal, and First Line teams so material incidents are assessed and notified to the relevant regulators on time, in line with Group and local regulatory expectations.

  • Enable the First Line: Give practical guidance on risk identification, assessment, incident reporting standards, and root-cause methodologies. Run workshops, training, and coaching so that RCSAs are a useful management tool rather than a compliance exercise and high-quality incident reporting becomes business as usual.

  • Maintain a clear 1LoD / 2LoD line: Keep ownership and accountability between First Line risk and control owners and Second Line oversight explicit and well documented.

You'll report to the Head of Operational Risk and work from our London or Amsterdam office three days a week.

What we're looking for

Essentials

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in operational risk management and controls within a financial services group, with proven experience in a Second Line (2LoD) capacity.

  • RCSA Programme Expertise: Experience designing, and implementing, RCSA programmes in a regulated financial services environment.

  • Control Design & Effectiveness: Strong understanding of control design and control effectiveness assessment, including how residual risk is rated and challenged.

  • Regulatory Acumen: Strong understanding of Group and local regulatory expectations relating to operational risk and control frameworks, and how to apply Group-wide methodologies to local entity requirements.

  • Data & Analytical Skills: Ability to analyse risk data, identify trends and emerging issues, and communicate findings clearly.

  • Facilitation & Stakeholder Management: Strong facilitation, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to challenge constructively and influence senior First Line leaders.

  • Documentation Discipline: Ability to produce clear, practical, and well-maintained framework documentation, standards, and guidance.

  • Direct experience building or deploying AI agents.

Preferred

  • Fintech / Hyper-Growth Background: Prior experience designing or scaling operational risk frameworks within a high-growth fintech, payments platform, or cloud-native technology company.

  • Multi-Entity / Global Exposure: Experience applying a Group framework across multiple legal entities, jurisdictions, and regulators.

  • Tooling Familiarity: Experience with GRC platforms and BI dashboards to support RCSA workflows, reporting, and action tracking.

  • Professional Background & Certifications: Prior experience in a Big Four / top-tier consultancy, alongside relevant qualifications such as CRISC, IRM Certificate, or equivalent.

You'll thrive here if

  • You're comfortable owning the roadmap yourself.

  • You own the outcome and you don't wait for permission to fix what's broken.

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity. Give you a problem, not a prescription, and you'll run with it.

  • You say what you mean. You're direct, but you lead with respect.

  • You simplify complexity rather than hiding behind it.

Applicant Safety Policy: Fraud and Third-Party Recruiters

To protect you from recruitment scams, please be aware that Airwallex will not ask for bank details, sensitive ID numbers (i.e. passport), or any form of payment during the application or interview process. All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page.

Airwallex will not pay any fees to search firms/recruiters if a candidate is submitted by a search firm/recruiter unless an agreement has been entered into with respect to specific open position(s). Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary.

Equal opportunity

Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. title: AVP, Data, Analytics & AI Engineering
descriptionHtml:
At Anaplan, we are a team of innovators focused on optimizing business decision-making through our leading AI-infused scenario planning and analysis platform so our customers can outpace their competition and the market.

What unites Anaplanners across teams and geographies is our collective commitment to our customers’ success and to our Winning Culture.

Our customers rank among the who’s who in the Fortune 50. Coca-Cola, LinkedIn, Adobe, LVMH and Bayer are just a few of the 2,400+ global companies who rely on our best-in-class platform.

Our Winning Culture is the engine that drives our teams of innovators. We champion diversity of thought and ideas, we behave like leaders regardless of title, we are committed to achieving ambitious goals, and we love celebratingour wins – big and small.

Supported by operating principles of being strategy-led, values-based and disciplined in execution, you’ll be inspired, connected, developed and rewarded here. Everything that makes you unique is welcome; join us and let’s build what’s next - together!

About the Role:

The AVP, Data, Analytics & AI Engineering is the executive leader responsible for the strategic vision, architecture, development, and scaling of our enterprise data platforms and AI solutions. This individual will lead a team tasked with turning enterprise data assets into high-performance, compliant, and secure intelligence frameworks that drive automation and strategic decision-making across the entire company. The role bridges the gap between modern cloud data stack engineering and emerging AI paradigms (like LLMOps and Agentic workflows). This individual will ensure that Anaplan engineering standards drive direct, measurable business value while maintaining top-tier data security, governance and responsible AI practices.

Your Impact

This is a critical role that requires an executive and organizational leader with a high degree of enterprise transformation leadership, discretion, and the ability to lead multiple priorities in a fast-paced, sales-driven, SaaS environment. This individual will work directly with the CFO, CRO, CHRO, CIO and Product leaders while building a high-performance engineering team.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Create Advanced Analytics/Decision Intelligence driving predictive analytics, propensity, forecasting, experimentation, causal thinking, optimization.
  • GenAI/Agent Engineering that is essential to the enterprise agent strategy – MCP, RAG, embeddings/vector search, tool calling, agent architecture, evaluation, grounding, orchestration. Architect and govern the Enterprise Agentic AI Strategy, deploying multi-agent frameworks and LLM-powered tools at scale.
  • Architect and deploy enterprise-grade multi-agent AI systems for complex, multi-step workflows, integrating with ERP, CRM, and ITSM to automate high-value decisions end-to-end.
  • Design internal AI tools and agents (e.g., AI Finance Bot, domain-specific LLM applications) and lead the roadmap for next-generation agentic platforms as emerging capabilities mature.
  • Drive Data Governance & AI Readiness – quality, lineage, observability, catalog, access controls, PII, retention, AI data governance.
  • Provide business context to a Semantic & Context Architecture with metrics layer, business ontology, entity relationships, metadata, knowledge graphs/semantic models.
  • Scale the team – build, mentor, motivate and lead high-performance team across Data Engineering, Analytics Engineering and AI Engineering.
  • Partner collaboratively with business units, product teams, security, legal and compliance teams to deliver AI and data solutions that align to enterprise goals.
  • Drive Anaplan beyond pipelines feeding dashboards into a Modern Data Architecture environment.

Your Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree, Computer Science, Data Engineering, AI/ML, Math or a highly quantitative field of study.
  • Leadership experience of 12+ years in data and software engineering environments, with at least 5 years in a senior manager or executive role leading cross-functional teams.
  • Strong familiarity with core technical stack - cloud data ecosystems (eg. Snowflake, Databricks, Vertex AI, AWS Sagemaker).
  • Experience moving to modern data architecture environment, with Deep Datawarehouse/lakehouse (AWS Redshift, Databricks), streaming/batch, APIs, data products, ELT, CDC, structured + unstructured data experience.
  • Proven experience with AI/ML engineering and success deploying ML models into production, feature engineering, model serving, monitoring, MLOps.
  • Exceptional ability to translate complex agentic systems, context-engineering strategies, and distributed database details into clear, business-relevant narratives for non-technical and executive boards.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB)

We believe attracting and retaining the best talent and fostering an inclusive culture strengthens our business. DEIB improves our workforce, enhances trust with our partners and customers, and drives business success. Build your career in a place where diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging aren’t just words on paper – this is what drives our innovation, it’s how we connect, and it contributes to what makes us a market leader. We believe in a hiring and working environment where all people are respected and valued, regardless of gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, age, neurodiversity, disability status, citizenship, or any other aspect which makes people unique. We hire you for who you are, and we want you to bring your authentic self to work every day! 

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, perform essential job functions, and receive equitable benefits and all privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.  

Fraud Recruitment Disclaimer  

It has come to our attention that fraudulent and fictitious job opportunities are being circulated on the Internet. Prospective candidates are being contacted by certain individuals, mainly through telephone calls, emails and correspondence, claiming they are representatives of Anaplan. The main purpose of these correspondences and announcements is to obtain privileged information from individuals.  

Anaplan does not:  

  • Extend offers to candidates without an extensive interview process with a member of our recruitment team and a hiring manager via video or in person.   
  • Send job offers via email. All offers are first extended verbally by a member of our internal recruitment team whenever possible and then followed up via written communication.  

All emails from Anaplan would come from an ----- email address. Should you have any doubts about the authenticity of an email, letter or telephone communication purportedly from, for, or on behalf of Anaplan, please send an email to ----- before taking any further action in relation to the correspondence.   

Privacy & AI Notice

Candidate data processed during our recruitment activities is handled in accordance with our Candidate Privacy Notice. This may include the use of artificial intelligence or automated tools to assist our team in evaluating qualifications.

title: Backend Engineer, AI Systems
descriptionHtml:
About ActAI

There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting.

Our first application is an agent-first mobile communication app. We believe building applications that users use daily for communication, coordination and collaboration needs will help integrate AI into their lives. The net effect is to eliminate misinformation, achieve low coordination costs, enable high quality tasks and collaboration at scale with minimal or little prompting.

 

Role

  • Build and maintain backend services and APIs for AI-powered applications

  • Develop inference orchestration systems that connect LLMs, application services and external tools

  • Design APIs for streaming responses, asynchronous processing and real-time interactions

  • Improve system performance through caching, batching, concurrency and database optimisation

  • Implement monitoring, logging, alerting and error handling for production services

  • Diagnose and resolve production issues involving latency, service failures and high traffic

  • Work with ML, frontend and mobile engineers on API design, system integration and deployment

 

Requirements

  • 3+ years of backend software engineering experience building production systems

  • Strong programming skills in Python, Node.js or similar backend technologies

  • Experience designing and maintaining REST or gRPC APIs, databases and distributed services

  • Understanding of asynchronous processing, concurrency, caching and message queues

  • Experience building scalable services and optimising latency, throughput and resource usage

  • Experience with SQL or NoSQL databases, Docker and cloud infrastructure

  • Ability to debug production issues using logs, metrics and distributed tracing

 

Nice to Have

  • Experience integrating LLM APIs, inference services or AI-powered applications

  • Experience with model serving, streaming inference or orchestration frameworks

  • Experience with Kubernetes and container orchestration

  • Familiarity with PyTorch, vLLM or open-source model deployment

  • Experience building real-time communication, messaging or high-traffic

title: CDI - Senior Context & Analytics Engineer - Paris
descriptionHtml:
Mission

Un agent ne vaut que ce que valent les données et les connaissances sur lesquelles il répond. Pipelines, modèles de données, définitions de métriques, droits d’accès : vous créez et gouvernez ce socle, et les applications et les agents de nos clients s’appuient dessus. Quand un analyste ou un agent demande un chiffre, la réponse est celle de l’équipe finance, accompagnée de sa définition et de sa source.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez que les métiers et les agents puissent se fier aux données, et les utilisent.

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype Context & Analytics Engineer.

Activités et responsabilités

Avec les équipes métier et les analystes, il s’agit de définir ce que signifie chaque métrique et de vérifier que les données y correspondent. Sur ce socle, les Product Engineers et les AI Engineers construisent applications et agents.

Les Platform Engineers exploitent l’infrastructure sur laquelle tournent vos pipelines. Les échanges avec les data owners et les équipes de gouvernance du client, la relecture de code entre pairs et l’accompagnement des nouvelles recrues complètent le quotidien.

Vos responsabilités :

  • Construire des pipelines d’ingestion et des modèles de données, avec dbt par exemple.
  • Mettre en place des contrôles de qualité des données et maintenir le lineage.
  • Construire la couche sémantique et les définitions de métriques, pour que les personnes et les agents utilisent les mêmes chiffres, y compris en text-to-SQL.
  • Définir les règles de gouvernance et les droits d’accès.
  • Construire des pipelines de connaissances pour le RAG : indexation, chunking, métadonnées, permissions.
  • Préparer le contexte exploitable par les agents : métadonnées, définitions, lineage et permissions.

Profil recherché

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous écrivez du SQL avec aisance et modélisez les données pour l’analyse.
  2. Des pipelines de données planifiés, testés et surveillés figurent à votre actif.
  3. Aux côtés des équipes métier, vous définissez les métriques et vérifiez que les données veulent bien dire ce que tout le monde croit y lire.
  4. La qualité des données, la documentation et les droits d’accès comptent pour vous.
  5. Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Python pour le traitement de données.
  • Une plateforme de données cloud, comme BigQuery, Snowflake ou Databricks.
  • Une couche sémantique ou un metrics store.
  • La préparation de documents pour le RAG : chunking, indexation, métadonnées.
  • Des outils de data catalogue ou de lineage.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Dans un métier où deux tableaux de bord affichent parfois deux chiffres différents, ce poste consiste à rétablir la confiance : un chiffre juste, une définition partagée, une source identifiable. Ce travail, discret quand il réussit, conditionne tout ce que les autres archétypes construisent au-dessus.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’apprend sur les projets, avec les AI Engineers et l’appui de la communauté Context & Analytics Engineer, notamment le context engineering, c’est-à-dire le travail qui rend les données exploitables par les agents d’IA. À partir de 2027, l’archétype Context & Analytics Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (évaluation de l’IA, responsabilité en production).

Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme les chapters AI Architect et AI Product Manager.

Processus de recrutement

Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.

  1. Entretien RH (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.
  2. Appel avec le CTO (15 à 30 min, à distance).
  3. Screening technique (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.
  4. Code review et live coding (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.
  5. Cas technique (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.
  6. Entretien final (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.

Selon les étapes, tous les outils d’IA sont autorisés, ou aucun. Lors du live coding, c’est la manière de travailler avec l’assistance de l’IA qui est observée.

Rémunération : 53 000€ à 63 000€ brut annuel (fixe) + jusqu’à 5 000€ de variable selon expérience et séniorité

Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l’adéquation avec le rôle.

This role is based in Vilnius, Lithuania. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our Vilnius office at least 3 days per week.

You must be a European citizen or already hold a valid right to work in Lithuania. We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Our process is designed to move fast:

title: Chemical Engineer (Solid Propellants)
descriptionHtml:
Chemical Engineer

We are looking for a Chemical Engineer to develop and improve the propellants and laboratory capability behind our solid rocket propulsion systems. You will combine practical laboratory work with engineering judgement, working on formulation, preparation, characterisation, incoming-material inspection, and the scale-up of propellant solutions from laboratory experiments to propulsion hardware.

About us

We’re a Germany-based rocketry startup currently in stealth mode, scaling up rapidly to meet the demand for high-performance, reliable, and scalable solid propulsion technologies for space and defense applications.

We are already launching suborbital and ballistic rockets on a regular basis, generating significant revenue and applying our knowledge toward the development of an orbital rocket.

We are working hard to build something truly spectacular.

To thrive here you will need to be comfortable working at pace, with the autonomy to make decisions and execute on them quickly. If you’re excited by hard technical challenges and want a role where you will make a real difference each day to the future of the company, we may be the place for you.

Key responsibilities

  • Develop, formulate, prepare, and improve solid propellants for different propulsion requirements.

  • Plan and conduct laboratory experiments, characterise materials, and document results clearly.

  • Work with propulsion engineers to connect formulation, processing, material properties, and motor performance.

  • Support incoming-goods inspection, supplier engagement, and the evaluation of specialist chemicals and raw materials.

  • Investigate unexpected results, non-conformances, processing issues, and material compatibility questions.

  • Improve laboratory procedures, equipment capability, data quality, safety, and the scale-up of successful formulations.

What we are looking for

  • A degree in chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, polymer science, energetic materials, or a related field.

  • Hands-on laboratory or process-development experience for solid propellants.

  • Strong understanding of chemistry, materials behaviour, experimental design, and laboratory safety.

  • A careful and methodical approach to traceability, measurement quality, process control, and documentation.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and a willingness to investigate unexpected results.

  • The ability to work collaboratively with propulsion, test, manufacturing, quality, and supplier teams.

Desirable experience

  • Solid rocket propellants, binders, oxidisers, metallic fuels, catalysts, or energetic materials.

  • Propellant characterisation, burn-rate measurement, thermal analysis, rheology, mechanical testing, ageing, or compatibility.

  • Scaling a formulation or laboratory process toward repeatable production.

  • Incoming-material inspection, chemical quality control, supplier qualification, or non-conformance investigation.

  • Hazardous chemicals, explosives, or regulated laboratory processes.

  • Laboratory data systems, statistical analysis, or Python-based data processing.

Benefits and important information:

  • We offer top-decile compensation packages, bonuses and meaningful equity, to attract exceptional aerospace talent.

  • Every employee is awarded stock options in the company, you will directly benefit from your own hard work and success.

  • Comprehensive relocation support including flights, shipping and visas.

  • Lunch, dinner and drinks provided everyday

  • Free access to shared company housing

Please note, we are a fast paced, hyper-scaling startup. You will need to be comfortable working extended hours with high levels of autonomy, ownership, and flexibility, with contracts structured around a 48-hour working week.

We are committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, has equal access to opportunity, and can thrive. We welcome different perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences—and believe our differences make us stronger.

  • A front-footed approach to AI and automation across reporting, forecasting, reconciliation and analysis

Who we're looking for

  • You've led finance before, or you're ready for your first shot and can prove it. A strong FD/Head of Finance ready to step up, or an early second-time CFO who wants to build rather than inherit. Either way, you can walk us through a function you built, not just one you worked inside.

  • You're commercial, not just technical. You read the business, not just the ledger, and have a view on where value is created and where it leaks.

  • You can build FP&A from scratch. Modelling, forecasting, scenario planning: the forward view is your craft, not something you outsource.

  • You're hands-on. You'll build it yourself before you delegate it, and you're not above the detail.

  • You're front-footed on tech and AI in finance. You already use modern tooling to make a lean function punch above its weight.

  • Experience in a marketplace, proptech, paytech, or subscription/usage-based B2B business

  • Direct experience leading or closely supporting a fundraise, refinancing or M&A process

What we offer

  • Real canvas. A proven, cash-generative business with the finance function still in its early innings: a de-risked model and a blank page.

  • Real mission. Our tech is quietly reshaping how the physical world of parking and mobility works.

  • Meaningful upside. A competitive package with a meaningful bonus and equity tied to what you build.

Why Hozah?

At Hozah, you'll play a pivotal role in a purpose-driven company at the forefront of urban mobility innovation. If you're looking to make a real difference in the future of mobility (and enjoy our friendly office dogs), we'd love to hear from you.

Tricks of the trade

Picnic Perks

You’ll receive an attractive compensation package, designed to reward your ambition, drive, and the direct impact you’ll make from your very first project.

🍎Learning & development 

You'll always have something to learn with us! You’ll benefit from opportunities like Lepaya training for polishing soft skills or Picnic Tech Academy training in case you want to learn new skills other than what you already know. At Picnic you get 30 holidays, we cover your travel expenses and offer a pension plan. And your phone and laptop are on us, of course.

FAQ

Which team will I join?

At Picnic, we build almost everything in-house. This means that we have plenty of opportunities for you in terms of project topics. Your interest lies in consumer topics like pricing, assortment, customer life time value? Or rather in logistics, supply chain, automated warehousing areas? Or you'd love going adventurous into new areas as long as you're solving real world problems? Let's talk and figure it out where there's the best match.  

What are the long term opportunities for this role? What happens after I'm done with a project?

You get full accountability from the start: from shaping the strategy and driving step-change improvements, to collaborating with multiple teams to achieve tangible business results.

At Picnic, the long-term opportunity isn't just a role—it’s a platform to shape your own career trajectory with real ownership, business impact, and fast growth.   • Given our scale-up environment, many projects tend to grow in scope and complexity under your responsibility and you naturally grow a team around you in order to take your project to a next level.
  • As you grow, you’ll deepen your understanding of the business, build a strong internal network, and prove your ability to lead impactful projects. Once you feel you’ve learned everything in your scope and your projects have been successfully implemented, you can switch to complete different areas of Picnic. We have numerous colleagues that have switched from Commercial to Fulfillment, or from Distribution to Customer and many other examples.

Please send your application in English.

title: Complaints Officer - Graduate
descriptionHtml:
About Lendable

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money.We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

  • One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people

  • Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK

  • Profitable since 2017

  • Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs

  • Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot)

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

  3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

About the role

This role is for someone wanting to start a career in operations within a financial services firm. You'll join as a Graduate focused on working complaints and train to become a fully competent Complaints Officer, investigating and resolving our more complex customer interactions across loans, cards and auto-finance. A critical role to help the business understand how it can serve customers better.

This is a casework role. From early on you will hold your own caseload, speak to customers directly, make decisions on whether we got it right, and put things right where we didn't. You will be supported through structured training, coaching and quality feedback as you develop in the role

Some of the areas you'll delve into are:

  • The regulatory framework for complaints: FCA regulation, the DISP rules, Consumer Duty, and how the guidance is applied to real cases.

  • Investigation technique: gathering evidence, interrogating system records and call recordings, and testing what actually happened against what should have happened.

  • Decision making and redress: reaching fair and objective outcomes, and calculating and explaining any compensation due.

  • Customer communication: writing final response letters that break complex issues down into plain English.

  • The Financial Ombudsman Service: how cases are referred, how FOS reaches its view, and how we apply those learnings to future cases.

  • Root cause and feedback: spotting the product and process failures behind complaints and feeding them back to frontline and product teams.

Reporting to a Complaints Manager within the Operations Team, you will be responsible for a live caseload and for the quality of the decisions you make on it.

No prior complaints experience needed, we care about how you think, not what you already know. This role requires an ability to learn quickly, work to deadlines and support our customers effectively.

Your team's objectives

Lendable aims to resolve all complaints promptly, ensuring that they are investigated diligently and fairly for customers. We are committed to providing excellent customer service and to reaching the right outcomes for our customers.

Feedback is an important part of how we evolve as a business. The team is encouraged to speak up, take each complaint on its own merits and provide valuable insight back into the business so we can improve and grow.

Our ability to handle complaints effectively for our customers and therefore for us as a business has never been more important than now, as we expand our existing products in the UK and US financial markets.

What you'll be doing

  • Investigating and resolving complaints about our loans, cards and auto-finance products, taking each case on its own merits

  • Self-managing a varied and increasingly complex caseload: prioritising cases, choosing the best contact mechanism for each customer, and working efficiently enough to meet our KPI minimum standards

  • Communicating with complainants in writing and by phone — managing expectations, handling difficult situations with tact and professionalism, and finding solutions to the issues raised

  • Writing professional final response letters that set out our decision, our rationale and the customer's right to refer to the Financial Ombudsman Service

  • Following our complaint handling standards and keeping clear records, making sure every decision is backed by demonstrable evidence and a documented rationale

  • Working to resolve complaints without the customer needing to refer to FOS, and applying the learnings from both internal and FOS outcomes to future cases

  • Feeding back to frontline and product teams on the product and process improvements your cases surface, across Operations and the wider Lendable business

  • Keeping your knowledge of Lendable's products current through effective use and review of our policies, procedures and business tools

  • Turning your hand to other areas of operational need as the business requires

What we're looking for

  • Educated to degree level

  • Exceptional written communication - you can structure an argument and explain a complex decision clearly to someone who is not an expert

  • An aptitude for investigation, analysis, problem-solving and dispute resolution

  • Strong organisation and self-management - you can hold a caseload, prioritise it and work to deadlines without being chased

  • Sound judgment and a sound moral compass: willing to speak up to make sure good customer outcomes stay at the heart of what we do

  • Resilience and adaptability in a fast-paced, changing environment

  • A willingness to learn FCA regulation and the DISP complaint handling rules and guidance

The interview process

We're not a corporation so we try our best to get things moving as quickly as possible. For this role we'd expect:

title: Customer Service and Sales administaror
descriptionHtml:
About Us

Cloverleaf Plumbing, Heating & Renewables is a well-established and growing business, proudly serving customers since 1994.

We specialise in plumbing, heating, air conditioning and renewable energy solutions, helping homeowners and businesses improve their comfort and energy efficiency.

As our business continues to grow, we're looking for an enthusiastic, organised and confident individual to join our friendly office team.

About the Role

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys working with people, thrives in a busy office environment, and wants to develop their career in customer relationship and sales.

Initially, the role will focus primarily on general office administration, customer service and supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the business.

However, we're looking for more than someone who simply processes paperwork.

You'll also play an important role in how we welcome new customers, manage incoming enquiries and guide prospective clients through the early stages of their journey with Cloverleaf.

As you become familiar with our services, systems and customers, there will be opportunities to take on greater sales responsibilities, develop your commercial skills and earn additional income through a commission structure.

You don't need to be a heating or renewable energy expert. We're much more interested in finding someone with the right personality, communication skills and willingness to learn.

Key Responsibilities

Office Administration & Operations

  • Manage and coordinate boiler and air source heat pump servicing, including customer reminders, bookings and follow-up communications.

  • Complete manufacturer product and warranty registrations, ensuring accurate records are maintained.

  • Assist with the administration of our company vehicle fleet, including servicing, MOTs, insurance and general vehicle records.

  • Maintain accurate customer information, job records and documentation within our Simpro management system.

  • Support the scheduling and coordination of engineers and customer appointments.

  • Liaise with customers, engineers, suppliers and other members of the team to ensure jobs progress smoothly.

  • Assist with general office administration and other operational tasks as required.

Customer Enquiries & Relationship Management

  • Act as a friendly, professional and confident first point of contact for customers contacting Cloverleaf by telephone, email or through our website.

  • Handle new sales enquiries, asking relevant questions to understand customers' requirements and identify the most appropriate next step.

  • Qualify and organise incoming enquiries, ensuring customers are directed towards the correct service, appointment or member of the team.

  • Build rapport with prospective customers and maintain communication throughout the early stages of their enquiry.

  • Arrange initial consultations, surveys and follow-up appointments with the appropriate team members.

  • Proactively follow up with prospective customers, keeping conversations moving forward and ensuring opportunities are not overlooked.

  • Maintain accurate customer notes and enquiry records to support a structured and professional sales process.

Sales Development & Career Progression

As you gain experience and confidence, we would like you to become increasingly involved in the commercial side of the business.

This could include:

  • Following up on quotations and helping customers make informed purchasing decisions.

  • Developing the confidence to discuss our services, explain their benefits and address common customer objections.

  • Managing your own customer enquiries and progressing opportunities through the sales process.

  • Helping convert enquiries into confirmed appointments and accepted quotations.

  • Working towards agreed sales targets with the opportunity to earn commission.

Full training and ongoing support will be provided as your responsibilities develop.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who combines excellent organisational skills with a natural ability to communicate and build relationships.

Essential Skills & Qualities

  • Previous experience in office administration, customer service or a similar role.

  • Confident, friendly and professional telephone manner.

  • Comfortable starting conversations with new customers and asking questions to understand their needs.

  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage several tasks and priorities.

  • Excellent attention to detail and a reliable approach to completing administrative work.

  • Good written communication and computer skills.

  • A proactive attitude, with the confidence to take ownership of tasks and follow them through.

  • Willingness to learn new systems, processes and technical information.

  • A positive, enthusiastic personality and the ability to work well within a small team.

  • An interest in developing customer relationship and sales skills.

Desirable Experience

  • Experience working in plumbing, heating, air conditioning, renewables, construction or a related industry.

  • Previous experience in a customer-facing sales or sales support role.

  • Experience using CRM or job management software such as Simpro.

  • Experience managing service schedules, customer appointments or maintenance contracts.

  • Previous involvement in following up on quotations or converting customer enquiries into sales.

Industry experience is an advantage but is not essential. We believe that the right attitude, personality and communication skills are just as important as previous technical knowledge.

What We Offer

  • Competitive basic salary of £26,000–£29,000 per annum, depending on experience.

  • Opportunity to earn additional sales commission as your role develops.

  • 20 days' annual leave plus 8 bank holidays.

  • An additional 3 days' paid holiday gifted by the company during our Christmas shutdown.

  • Workplace pension scheme.

  • Friendly, supportive and established team environment.

  • Training on our products, services and business systems.

  • Genuine opportunities for professional development as the company continues to grow.

  • The opportunity to play an important role in a growing business within the renewable energy sector.

How to Apply

If you're organised, enjoy speaking with people and would like a role that offers both variety and the opportunity to develop your career, we'd love to hear from you.

We're particularly interested in hearing from candidates who are confident on the telephone, enjoy building customer relationships and are motivated to take on more responsibility over time.

Please apply with your up-to-date CV and a brief introduction explaining why you feel you'd be a good fit for our team.

title: Customer Success Manager
descriptionHtml:
Customer Success Manager

Location: Remote (European/UK time zones) - French and English required

About FullEnrich:

Every go-to-market motion runs on data, but no single provider has ever had complete coverage. We solve that problem: instead of relying on a single data source, we orchestrate 20+ premium providers around the world, automatically querying them and verifying data in real-time until we find the best available contact information. The result is industry-leading coverage and data quality, helping sales and GTM teams connect with the right people faster.

What started as a better way to find emails and phone numbers has grown into a broader vision: becoming the trusted GTM data infrastructure layer powering modern revenue teams and AI agents. Today, more than 6,000 customers, including companies like AWS, Deel, HubSpot, Clay, Intercom, Unify,and Artisan, trust us to power their prospecting and enrichment.

Founded in Paris and now headquartered in San Francisco, we're a team of 50+ people across the US, Europe, LATAM, and Israel, growing quickly and building with speed, ownership, and ambition. That's where you come in.

The Role:

You’ll be joining as a Customer Success Manager in our Customer Success team, reporting to Jemima, our Founding CSM.

FullEnrich has grown to 5,000+ customers, and our CS function has been a team of one until now. We're bringing in our next CSM to own all of our French-speaking customers, across every segment, plus our Scale/SMB book ($10k to $25k ARR). Day to day, you'll onboard new customers, drive adoption, run renewals end to end, and spot the accounts that are ready to grow. Ownership here means your book is yours: you know every account, you close every renewal, and you catch risk before it turns into churn. You'll work closely with Sales, Product and Support, and because the team is still small, you'll help shape the playbooks the rest of CS is built on.

What You'll Do:

Own your book

  • Own the post-sale relationship for all of our French-speaking customers who range from Enterprise to SMB, plus our Scale/SMB book

  • Run onboarding and kick-off calls so new customers reach first value quickly

  • Be the voice of your customers internally, feeding product feedback into the roadmap

Renewals & retention

  • Own renewals end to end: forecasting, commercial conversations and closing

  • Monitor usage, credit consumption and health signals, and act early on risk

  • Run save plays on at-risk accounts before renewal is on the line

Adoption & expansion

  • Drive adoption across our API, CSV/bulk upload and CRM integrations

  • Identify and qualify expansion opportunities, then hand them to Sales with full context

Scaled CS

  • Contribute to one-to-many programs: French-language webinars, office hours and enablement content

  • Help improve our playbooks and keep HubSpot data clean and reliable

What Success Looks like:

By 3 months

  • Confident across the product (API, CSV, integrations) and our CS playbooks

  • Owning your full book, with every account health-scored and a main point of contact in HubSpot

  • Running renewals independently, and you have hosted your first French-language webinar or office hours

By 6 months

  • Book on track for 90%+ gross revenue retention

  • [X]% of the book active and healthy (target to confirm once the health score is defined)

  • A steady flow of qualified expansion handoffs to Sales

By 12 months

  • 90%+ GRR delivered across the book

  • Measurable improvement in adoption and health across the book

  • The trusted internal voice on our French-speaking customers, shaping how we scale CS

What We're Looking For:

  • Native-level French and fluent English, written and spoken

  • 2 to 4 years in a SaaS Customer Success role, owning a book of business

  • A track record of owning and closing renewals, not just managing relationships

  • Comfortable running a high-volume book and prioritising with data

  • At home in a CRM (HubSpot ideally) and using usage data to make decisions

  • Warm, clear communicator who's confident in commercial conversations

  • Builder mindset: you like a fast-growing team where the playbook is still being written

Nice to Haves

  • Background in B2B data, sales tech or GTM tooling

  • Comfortable talking APIs and integrations with technical buyers

  • Confident using Claude to speed up your day-to-day work

The Hiring Process:

  • Intro to FullEnrich with our Talent Team (30 min) – A chance to learn more about you, introduce FullEnrich and the role, and explore whether there's a mutual fit.

title: Deployed Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Wordsmith

Wordsmith is building the legal operating system for in-house teams, and we are growing fast.

We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents and disconnected systems.

Wordsmith brings that work into one system. Requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgement matters, and every step is captured as work happens.

We are built for in-house legal, not law firms. Our goal is to help legal teams move faster, reduce unnecessary external counsel spend and become a function the business can run with.

More than 500 companies, including Financial Times, Safelite, Trip.com, Canva, Starling and Sage, use Wordsmith. Backed by over $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe and others, we are building one of the defining companies in legal AI.

The role

Deployment Engineers own the technical side of getting Wordsmith live inside a customer.

Once a deal is signed, you’ll connect Wordsmith to the systems our customers already run on. That means identity and SSO, Microsoft 365 and SharePoint, Google Workspace, Salesforce, document management, chat tools, and MCP connections to the wider AI and data stack. You’ll design how data and permissions flow between them, build and test the integrations, and work through each customer’s IT and security requirements until everything works in production.

It’s part integration engineering, part solutions architecture, and part customer-facing problem solving. You’ll be the technical lead on every deployment you own, the person customer IT teams talk to, and the person who works out how to make it work when an integration doesn’t behave as documented.

This is a technical, hands-on role. You don’t need to be a lawyer, and we’re not necessarily looking for one. We’re looking for engineers and technical consultants who understand identity, APIs and enterprise SaaS, and who enjoy making systems talk to each other. Your focus is the technical foundation the rest of the deployment runs on.

You’ll work side by side with our Legal Engineers on every deployment. While you connect Wordsmith to the customer’s systems, they configure the platform itself: workflows, agents, playbooks and automations built around how the legal team works. You’ll plan the deployment together, agree what each integration needs to support, and make sure the connections you build give their configuration the data, documents and permissions it depends on.

What you’ll do

1. Integrations

  • Own the integrations for each deployment, including SSO and SCIM, Microsoft 365, SharePoint and OneDrive, Google Workspace, Salesforce, document management and chat tools

  • Configure and connect Wordsmith to customers’ wider AI and data stack through MCP

  • Build, test and harden integrations so they hold up in production, not just in a demo

2. Identity, Security & Access

  • Set up identity and access, including SSO with Okta, Entra ID and Google, user provisioning, roles and permissions

  • Work through customers’ security reviews, IT questionnaires and data-handling requirements

  • Make sure permissions in Wordsmith respect the permissions in the systems it connects to

3. Technical Solution Design

  • Take the technical handover from Sales and confirm the customer’s systems landscape, constraints and integration scope

  • Design how data, documents and requests flow between Wordsmith and the customer’s tools

  • Advise customer IT on the right architecture for their environment and where the trade-offs sit

  • Work with Legal Engineers to agree what each integration needs to support the workflows, agents and playbooks they’re configuring

4. Technical Delivery & Escalation

  • Lead the technical workstream of each deployment, from environment setup and integration build through testing to go-live

  • Diagnose and fix integration issues, and act as the escalation point for technical problems during rollout

  • Know when a problem needs Engineering, and bring them a clear, reproducible case

5. Improve How We Integrate

  • Turn what you learn into reusable integration patterns, setup guides and technical runbooks

  • Feed connector gaps, API limitations and recurring requests back to Product and Engineering

What we’re looking for

  • Hands-on experience deploying and integrating enterprise SaaS in customer environments

  • Strong working knowledge of identity and access, including SSO (SAML, OIDC), SCIM provisioning, Okta, Entra ID or Google Workspace

  • Experience integrating with the Microsoft 365 and SharePoint, Google Workspace or Salesforce ecosystems

  • Comfortable with APIs, webhooks, authentication flows and reading technical documentation. You can script or write code where it helps

  • Familiarity with MCP or other ways of connecting AI systems to tools and data, or a strong appetite to learn

  • Credible with customer IT and security teams. You can answer their questions and stand behind your architecture

  • Methodical troubleshooter who isolates problems, reproduces them and fixes them

  • Clear communicator who can explain a technical decision to a non-technical stakeholder

Typical backgrounds include

  • Deployment, integration or implementation engineers in SaaS

  • Solutions engineers or solutions architects

  • Technical consultants with Microsoft 365, Google Workspace or Salesforce experience

  • IT or identity engineers who have moved into customer-facing roles

How we work

We’re an in-person team based in Edinburgh or London. You should expect to work from the office or visit customers as your default.

We set a high bar, move quickly and give people meaningful ownership. There will not always be an established playbook, so you’ll need to bring curiosity, structure and persistence to unfamiliar situations.

You’ll sit in the Transformation team, reporting to the VP of Transformation, and work closely with our Legal Engineers, alongside Legal Intelligence, Enablement, Customer Success, Support Engineering and Product.

Our customer teams have clear but closely connected responsibilities: Transformation leads implementation, Support Engineering resolves technical issues, Account Management owns renewals and commercial growth, Customer Success owns adoption, customer health and value realisation, and Enablement owns onboarding, training and customer capability.

Why Wordsmith

Wordsmith is growing quickly, winning new customers and expanding within larger organisations. Wordsmith is only as useful as the systems it connects to. Every new customer brings a different stack, and Deployment Engineers are the people who make Wordsmith work inside it.

You’ll work directly with ambitious in-house legal teams, see how dozens of legal functions really operate, and take that back into a product you help shape. You will work across enterprise identity, productivity and CRM platforms, and on MCP as it develops into a standard. You will own real technical outcomes from your first week and help define how we integrate as we scale.

title: Deployment Strategist - German Speaking
descriptionHtml:
About HappyRobot

HappyRobot is the infrastructure for enterprises to build and orchestrate AI workforces. Our AI workers don't just communicate through voice and email - they make decisions, take action, and run operations autonomously across entire enterprise systems. Born in Y Combinator (S23) and backed by a16z, Base10, Prysm Capital and Eurazeo with over $200M raised, we power critical operations for global enterprises worldwide.

Our platform is battle-tested in the most demanding environments, where AI has real consequences. We started in logistics, built our own voice stack, models, and orchestration layer from the ground up, and are now bringing that infrastructure to every enterprise that runs the real economy. Learn more about our vision in our manifesto.

Role Overview

We are looking for a Deployment Strategist to join our team. In this role, you'll partner with Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) across the full deployment lifecycle, from first discovery conversation to live production. You'll lead use case discovery and scoping with senior customer stakeholders, ship prototypes hands-on to prove value early, then stay close to the build through delivery to bring the strategic, business-value lens to every decision. You're the partner who keeps the work pointed at the highest-impact outcomes, ready to pick up the keyboard alongside the FDE when the moment calls for it.

We're looking for engineers with strategic instincts: people who can write code, but whose deepest strength is the strategic, opinionated lens they bring across every phase of a deployment - spotting where value lives, scoping it realistically, and partnering with engineers to capture it from prototype to production.

At HappyRobot, there's no role seniority or hierarchy. We operate as a team of builders. We execute, we build, we own, and we care deeply about our customers and their success.

What You'll do

  • Strategic Leadership and Use Case Discovery: Partner with Global and Regional C-Level executives and VPs to assess AI opportunities and prioritize the highest-impact use cases. Lead curiosity-driven discovery that surfaces the workflows where AI creates the most business value, well beyond what the customer thought to ask for. Build the trusted relationships that let you present findings and challenge assumptions at the most senior levels, keeping technical delivery aligned with their business priorities.

  • Scoping: Frame impact versus effort with rigor on both axes. On business value, pressure-test the realistic upside, question whether the use case as posed will actually deliver the most impact, and explore whether reframing it or pivoting to an adjacent process would unlock more. The art is deeply understanding how to maximize value of this use case for the customer, not just delivering what was asked for. On technical effort, map integrations, data, and platform constraints, and surface the edge cases and dependencies that shape timelines. Land on a plan that's realistic on both.

  • Prototyping: Build prototypes and demos hands-on. Use our platform and AI-powered coding tools to test ideas end-to-end at light scope. Prove value early, before the customer commits.

  • Program Management: Coordinate work across the active deployments in an account. Be the escalation point for the customer and the watchout partner for the FDE. Stay close enough to the build that you both understand the use case deeply, spot opportunities to capture more value, and catch when work is drifting from the highest-impact path.

  • Prioritization: Sequence use cases within an account so each deployment compounds the next. Make the call on what gets built when, what gets parked, and where to invest discovery and building time.

  • Customer Partnership: Be the main business-side point of contact for the account. Build trust with operational and executive stakeholders day-to-day. Translate AI capabilities into language they can act on.

  • Onsite Embedding: Travel onsite for kickoffs, mapping sessions, and key moments where being on the ground changes the outcome.

  • Product Feedback Loop: Bring field signal back to Product and Engineering. Identify reusable patterns, common edge cases, and where the platform needs to evolve.

Must Have

  • Background that mixes technical depth with strategic instinct, and a real history of building things. Common paths include engineering (Computer Science, electrical, industrial, systems), data science, founding a tech startup, product management, or technical / strategic consulting.

  • Comfortable coding -mostly Python- using LLMs and AI-powered tools like Claude Code to ship prototypes fast.

  • Working understanding of APIs, integrations, and how AI agents sit inside enterprise workflows.

  • Strategic instinct: ability to spot the business value behind a workflow and translate it into impact, effort, and prioritization terms a C-level can act on.

  • Excellent communication skills with both executives and operators. Comfortable translating between business and technical without losing either side.

  • Proven ability to prioritize ruthlessly across multiple workstreams and drive outcomes, not just activity.

  • Founder mindset: highly independent, takes ownership, and thrives in a fast-paced environment.

Why join us?

  • Join a world-class team of engineers and builders.

  • Backed by top investors including a16z, Y Combinator, Base10, Prysm Capital and Eurazeo.

  • Have ownership and autonomy of projects and are encouraged to ship.

  • Comprehensive Benefits including healthcare, dental, vision coverage.

  • Competitive salary + equity in a high-growth startup.

Our Operating Principles

Extreme Ownership

We take full responsibility for our work, outcomes, and team success. No excuses, no blame-shifting — if something needs fixing, we own it and make it better. This means stepping up, even when it’s not “your job.” If a ball is dropped, we pick it up. If a customer is unhappy, we fix it. If a process is broken, we redesign it. We don’t wait for someone else to solve it — we lead with accountability and expect the same from those around us.

Craftsmanship

Putting care and intention into every task, striving for excellence, and taking deep ownership of the quality and outcome of your work. Craftsmanship means never settling for “just fine.” We sweat the details because details compound. Whether it’s a product feature, an internal doc, or a sales call — we treat it as a reflection of our standards. We aim to deliver jaw-dropping customer experiences by being curious, meticulous, and proud of what we build — even when nobody’s watching.

We are “majos”
Be friendly & have fun with your coworkers. Always be genuine & honest, but kind. “Majo” is our way of saying: be a good human. Be approachable, helpful, and warm. We’re building something ambitious, and it’s easier (and more fun) when we enjoy the ride together. We give feedback with kindness, challenge each other with respect, and celebrate wins together without ego.

Urgency with Focus
Create the highest impact in the shortest amount of time. Move fast, but in the right direction. We operate with speed because time is our most limited resource. But speed without focus is chaos. We prioritize ruthlessly, act decisively, and stay aligned. We aim for high leverage: the biggest results from the simplest, smartest actions. We’re running a high-speed marathon — not a sprint with no strategy.

Talent Density and Meritocracy
Hire only people who can raise the average; ‘exceptional performance is the passing grade.’ Ability trumps seniority. We believe the best teams are built on talent density — every hire should raise the bar. We reward contribution, not titles or tenure. We give ownership to those who earn it, and we all hold each other to a high standard. A-players want to work with other A-players — that’s how we win.

First-Principles Thinking
Strip a problem to physics-level facts, ignore industry dogma, rebuild the solution from scratch. We don’t copy-paste solutions. We go back to basics, ask why things are the way they are, and rebuild from the ground up if needed. This mindset pushes us to innovate, challenge stale assumptions, and move faster than incumbents. It’s how we build what others think is impossible.

Aerospace demand is surging. OEMs have decade-long backlogs, new manufacturers are racing to market, and the industry is hundreds of thousands of technicians short.

The world needs more aerospace capacity, but the systems used to maintain and manufacture aircraft are slow, manual, and barely changed in decades. Fleetcraft is the full system to operate and manage aircraft maintenance. Our agents already work alongside technicians and controllers in 10+ maintenance organisations across 4 continents. Our seed was led by Susa Ventures, alongside Liquid 2 VC, early backers of Anduril and Stoke Space. The role

As a Deployment Strategist, you’ll own customer implementation end-to-end.

You’ll translate complex operational requirements into AI-solutions, work hands-on with customers to drive adoption, and turn what you learn in the field into sales and engineering priorities.

This is a highly hands-on, high-ownership role. You’ll work directly with technicians, operators, managers, and executives to understand their workflows, deploy Fleetcraft into live environments, and make sure the product becomes mission-critical.

We’re looking for someone with exceptional learning velocity, commercial instinct, and technical competence. You should be pragmatic, intentional, and very structured. Aerospace experience is not required - the ability to learn quickly, adapt, and handle complex implementations with high emotional intelligence.

What we offer

£75k–£110k salary plus meaningful early-stage equity.

A small, high-trust team where your decisions move the whole company forward. Relocation support if needed. Modern tools, real-world impact in a regulated industry, and the chance to define how AI transforms aerospace from the ground up.

If you're energised by building production AI systems that solve hard, real-world problems - and you want the ownership and pace that only comes from being early at something important, we'd love to talk.

title: Director Accounting & Finance - FTC
descriptionHtml:
Who We Are:
At Omaze, we give our community in the UK and Germany the chance to win luxury homes and other life-changing prizes — all while raising money for the causes they love.

Thanks to our Omaze Community, we’ve raised over £150 million for UK charities in just five years. That’s millions helping organisations like Age UK, the RSPCA, British Heart Foundation and Great Ormond Street Hospital Charity deliver life-saving work.

And the best part? We’re only just getting started. Omaze is building a business and culture committed to growth and creating significant social impact on a global scale.

🔑 About The Job

We’re looking for an experienced, hands-on accounting and finance leader to provide maternity cover of 14 months during a period of continued business development and finance transformation.

This is a broad role combining financial reporting, month-end delivery, cash and debt-facility reporting, corporate governance support and finance-systems ownership. You’ll work closely with the CFO, Finance and Accounting colleagues, business leaders and external advisers to maintain reliable reporting, effective controls and continuity across key workstreams.

You’ll be equally comfortable reviewing accounting entries, explaining budget variances, coordinating an audit and resolving a NetSuite reporting or access issue. Success will mean keeping essential processes running smoothly while progressing agreed improvements and making risks, decisions and dependencies visible.

🥇 What success looks like

  • Month-end close, consolidated reporting and board-reporting inputs are delivered accurately and on time.

  • Lender reporting and compliance requirements are met, with clear oversight of deadlines and dependencies.

  • Budget holders receive useful analysis and timely support.

  • Audit and adviser workstreams progress with clear ownership and well-organised evidence.

  • Finance systems remain reliable, and agreed implementation and reporting improvements continue.

  • Responsibilities, decisions and outstanding matters are documented to support a smooth handover back.

🔧 What You’ll Be Doing

Audit, governance, tax and technical accounting

  • Coordinate audit delivery, acting as a central contact for auditors and internal stakeholders and tracking evidence requests, issues and deadlines.

  • Draft consolidated and entity level financial statements along with relevant footnote disclosures under IFRS and US GAAP.

  • Initiate implementation of IFRA 18 and ASU 2024-03.

  • Support corporate governance processes and associated financial documentation and reporting.

  • Support the CFO with Senior Accounting Officer (SAO) and Corporate Criminal Offence (CCO) workstreams, including documentation, information gathering and follow-through on agreed actions.

  • Coordinate accounting advisory workstreams, ensuring clear briefs, ownership, timely responses and resolution of outstanding matters.

  • Ad hoc technical accounting assessments, documenting agreed conclusions and supporting implementation.

Financial accounting, close and consolidated reporting

  • Deliver assigned month-end close activities, including intercompany eliminations, and coordinate with entity accounting teams.

  • Prepare and coordinate consolidated monthly financial reporting under US GAAP and IFRS, ensuring completeness, consistency and clear explanations of significant movements.

  • Review assigned journals, reconciliations and intercompany activity, resolving issues with the relevant preparers and reviewers.

  • Maintain close timetables, support the resolution of blockers and ensure appropriate documentation and review evidence.

  • Support the preparation and validation of financial actuals and analysis for board reporting.

Equity administration and insurance

  • Administer Carta, including reporting, supporting bookkeeping, maintaining records and coordinating approved changes with relevant stakeholders.

  • Coordinate corporate, office and other insurance matters, working with brokers, Legal and business owners on renewals, coverage questions, policy changes and emerging requirements.

  • Maintain clear records of outstanding actions, approvals and responsibilities across both workstreams.

Finance systems and reporting

  • Act as the day-to-day Netsuite administrator, covering month-end requirements, ongoing maintenance, user access, configuration and issue resolution.

  • Facilitate work with external Netsuite support partners, prioritising requests and coordinating delivery, testing and implementation.

  • Develop and maintain Netsuite reporting for Finance, including reports and saved searches that improve visibility and reduce manual work.

  • Administer and maintain Netsuite Account Reconciliation system, including period roll-forwards, assignments and troubleshooting.

Cash, treasury and loan facility reporting

  • Coordinate monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting, certificates, utilisation requests and other required submissions, including event-triggered reporting.

  • Maintain a clear compliance calendar and work with the CFO, Legal and Accounting teams to ensure timely, accurate reporting and escalation.

🤩 About You

Essential experience and skills

  • A recognised accounting qualification ACA, ACCA, CPA or equivalent.

  • Experience drafting consolidated and entity-level financial statements under both IFRS and US GAAP.

  • Strong experience across financial accounting, consolidated reporting and month-end close in a multi-national environment.

  • Strong hands-on NetSuite experience, including administration, reporting and working with external support partners.

  • Experience coordinating external audits and managing relationships with professional advisers.

  • Confidence managing cash reporting, debt-facility reporting and compliance deadlines.

  • Sound technical accounting judgement, with the ability to identify when specialist advice or escalation is needed.

  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise competing operational and project demands and supporting Accounting and Finance team members.

  • Clear communication and the confidence to challenge constructively, explain complex issues and drive actions to completion.

Desirable experience

  • UK and US accounting and reporting requirements, including US GAAP and IFRS.

  • NSAR and NSPB administration or implementation.

  • Carta and equity-related accounting or administration.

  • Senior Accounting Officer support (familiarity with Criminal Finance Act), insurance coordination or corporate governance support.

  • Subscription, e-commerce or other high-volume transaction businesses.

🙌 What’s In It For You

  • 25 days annual leave PLUS Bank Holidays

  • Private medical and dental insurance

  • 9% employer pension contributions, when you contribute at least 2%

  • A generous personal learning and development budget each year to use on training courses, conferences and professional memberships

  • Enhanced family leave policies

  • Life assurance of 4x your salary

DEI Statement

We actively seek out diversity of thought and experience to drive innovation. We welcome all backgrounds, identities, and perspectives and work hard to ensure that every Omaze employee can bring their authentic self to work at all times.
